title: The mechanism of honeysuckle peptides in ameliorating hyperuricemia in mice via the PGC-1alpha/PPARgamma/ABCG2 pathway.
authors: Yang, Hongxuan; Liang, Yun; Chen, Yue'e; Liu, Lin; Wang, Yingfang; Dou, Qiting; Gong, Jinmei; Liao, Zijing; Dong, Junqiu; Hu, Xuguang
one_liner_zh: 该文研究金银花肽通过PGC-1alpha/PPARgamma/ABCG2通路改善小鼠高尿酸血症，涉及分子对接但核心为代谢疾病药理与肠道菌群，非蛋白质-DNA互作或TF-DNA结合机制，与本课题无关。
abstract: ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: Lonicera japonica Thunb (honeysuckle), a traditional Chinese medicine, has been historically used to clear heat, detoxify, and dispel wind-heat. Modern research has identified various bioactive constituents from honeysuckle, supporting its potential in managing inflammatory and metabolic disorders. However, the anti-hyperuricemic activity and mechanism of its peptide components remain unexplored. AIM OF THE STUDY: This study aimed to investigate the anti-hyperuricemic effect of honeysuckle-derived peptides and the underlying mechanisms, with a focus on uric acid production, excretion, and gut microbiota modulation. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Nine novel peptides were identified from honeysuckle by HPLC-MS/MS and screened through molecular docking against xanthine oxidase (XOD). In vitro XOD inhibition and antioxidant assays were performed. A hyperuricemic mouse model was induced by potassium oxonate and hypoxanthine. Mice were treated with honeysuckle peptides at low, medium, and high doses. Serum biomarkers, renal and ileal histopathology, protein and mRNA expression of PGC-1alpha/PPARgamma/ABCG2 pathway components, and gut microbiota composition (16S rRNA sequencing) were analyzed. RESULTS: Molecular docking confirmed strong binding between the peptides and XOD. In vitro, honeysuckle peptides significantly inhibited XOD activity and exhibited potent antioxidant capacity. In vivo, peptide treatment effectively reduced serum uric acid, XOD, creatinine, and blood urea nitrogen levels, alleviated renal and intestinal tissue damage, and suppressed inflammatory cytokines. The treatment also significantly upregulated the renal PGC-1alpha/PPARgamma/ABCG2 pathway at both protein and mRNA levels. Furthermore, the peptides restored gut microbial diversity and corrected the Firmicutes/Bacteroidota ratio. CONCLUSION: Honeysuckle peptides ameliorate hyperuricemia through a dual mechanism: inhibiting uric acid production by suppressing XOD activity and promoting its renal excretion by activating the PGC-1alpha/PPARgamma/ABCG2 pathway, coupled with restoring gut microbiota homeostasis. This study provides a pharmacological basis for the traditional use of honeysuckle and highlights its peptides as promising candidates for managing hyperuricemia.
abstract_zh: 民族药理学相关性：金银花（Lonicera japonica Thunb），一种传统中药，历史上用于清热、解毒和疏散风热。现代研究已从金银花中鉴定出多种生物活性成分，支持其在管理炎症和代谢性疾病方面的潜力。然而，其肽类成分的抗高尿酸血症活性及机制尚未被探索。研究目的：本研究旨在探讨金银花来源肽的抗高尿酸血症效应及其潜在机制，重点关注尿酸生成、排泄和肠道菌群调节。材料与方法：通过HPLC-MS/MS从金银花中鉴定出九种新型肽，并针对黄嘌呤氧化酶（XOD）进行分子对接筛选。进行了体外XOD抑制和抗氧化测定。通过氧嗪酸钾和次黄嘌呤诱导高尿酸血症小鼠模型。小鼠分别接受低、中、高剂量的金银花肽处理。分析了血清生物标志物、肾脏和回肠组织病理学、PGC-1alpha/PPARgamma/ABCG2通路组分的蛋白和mRNA表达，以及肠道菌群组成（16S rRNA测序）。结果：分子对接确认了肽与XOD之间的强结合。体外实验中，金银花肽显著抑制XOD活性并表现出强抗氧化能力。体内实验中，肽处理有效降低了血清尿酸、XOD、肌酐和血尿素氮水平，减轻了肾脏和肠道组织损伤，并抑制了炎症细胞因子。该处理还在蛋白和mRNA水平上显著上调了肾脏PGC-1alpha/PPARgamma/ABCG2通路。此外，肽恢复了肠道微生物多样性并纠正了Firmicutes/Bacteroidota比例。结论：金银花肽通过双重机制改善高尿酸血症：通过抑制XOD活性减少尿酸生成，通过激活PGC-1alpha/PPARgamma/ABCG2通路促进其肾脏排泄，同时恢复肠道菌群稳态。本研究为金银花的传统用途提供了药理学基础，并强调其肽类作为管理高尿酸血症的有前景候选物。
